stories.headline: Bihar Man Dies After Flood Relief Packet Dropped From Helicopter Hits Him
stories.title: Bihar Man Dies After Flood Relief Packet Dropped From Helicopter Hits Him
stories.summary: The body has been sent to a hospital for post-mortem
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday targeted the BJP-led government over Bihar’s recurring flood crisis, asking what had changed on the ground in the last 17 years and calling for a permanent solution instead of yearly relief and assurances.

In a post on X, while offering his condolences Rahul said that floods had once again struck Bihar with “devastating force”, affecting millions, submerging hundreds of villages and leaving several people dead or missing.
“The most heartbreaking thing is that this crisis in Bihar is not new,” Rahul said, pointing to the recurring cycle of floods, deaths, shattered families and migration.
“The BJP's double-engine government should tell us — what has it done in the last 17 years to address this annual tragedy?
What has changed on the ground?” he asked.
Rahul said people in Bihar did not need relief and assurances every year but a permanent solution to the recurring floods.
The latest flood spell affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts, according to the Bihar disaster management department.
The affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.

The floods came amid heavy rainfall in Bihar and neighbouring areas, with officials saying water levels in the Ganga, Sone and Gandak rose sharply after heavy rain in Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, as well as rainfall in the catchment areas of rivers originating in Nepal.
This year's flooding also differed from the usual pattern.
While the Kosi and Gandak were responsible for the first two flood spells, the prolonged third spell in September was mainly driven by the swollen Ganga, Sone and Punpun rivers.
The Bihar government has stepped up relief operations, with chief minister Samrat Choudhary saying the administration would ensure assistance reached affected families.

stories.headline: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
stories.title: Gyanesh Kumar undermined Election Commission’s independence: Sachin Pilot
stories.summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot alleged the SIR is being used to selectively delete voters, as he also criticised the Rajasthan government’s drought response and the AAP government in Punjab
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Sunday (October 4, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the independence of the Election Commission, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was being used to selectively delete voters.

Talking to reporters in Jaipur, Mr. Pilot alleged that Mr. Kumar had sidelined the other two Election Commissioners while taking decisions related to the electoral roll revision, and demanded action against him.
“India and the country function according to law.
The Election Commission has three members, and decisions are taken either unanimously or by a majority.
But Gyanesh Kumar sidelined the other two Election Commissioners and started the entire process on his own,” he alleged.
Mr. Pilot claimed that powers normally exercised by Electoral Registration.
Officers (EROs) at the local level were being centralised, and alleged that names of voters were being added or deleted from Delhi.
He claimed about 13 crore names had been removed from electoral rolls across the country, and alleged that voters were being selectively targeted in States including Haryana, Bihar and West Bengal.
“First there was demonetisation, and now they are doing ‘votebandi’.
Voting is the biggest democratic right of a citizen.
If that right is taken away, what could be more serious than this?” Mr. Pilot said.
He alleged that public confidence in the Election Commission as an impartial constitutional institution had been eroded, and demanded action against the CEC.

stories.headline: Can't Have An Election Commission Which Malfunctions Like This; Supreme Court Must Decide CEC Case Soon : Justice Nariman
stories.title: Can't Have An Election Commission Which Malfunctions Like This; Supreme Court Must Decide CEC Case Soon : Justice Nariman
stories.summary: "The heart of the Constitution and the heart of democracy, which is the right to vote, is at great peril," Justice Nariman said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "The heart of the Constitution and the heart of democracy, which is the right to vote, is at great peril," Justice Nariman said.

Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman, former Supreme Court judge, expressed serious reservations over the functioning of the Election Commission of India, in the light of the massive disenfranchisement of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the reports which suggested that several crucial decisions were taken by the Chief Election Commissioner, ignoring the objections of the other two Election Commissioners.
"You can't have an election commission which functions or malfunctions like this," he said.
He lamented that the disenfranchisement of 90 lakh voters in West Bengal had not moved the Supreme Court sufficiently to stay the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Justice Nariman also described leaving the appointment of Election Commissioners entirely in the hands of the government of the day as a "red flag", warning that it had put the right to vote at great peril.
He stressed that the Supreme Court must decide the validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act (CEC Act) at the earliest.

He further expressed disappointment over the Supreme Court's two-judge bench delivering a split verdict on the challenge to the appointment process of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners, saying that it had allowed the government to continue making appointments under a process involving substantial executive influence.

Justice Nariman was speaking on 'The Constitution and the Common Man' at the Rajkumar College, Rajkot, where he stated that the right to vote for a common man is under threat nowadays because of the damage the government has done to the ECI.
He said that Chapter XV was added to the Constitution to ensure that the vote of every citizen actually translates into something meaningful for the government that the person has chosen.
However, the independence and impartiality of the CEC are under question since its appointment and removal were at the hands of the government.
Therefore, in Anoop Baranwal.

Union of India(2023), the Supreme Court, as a pro tem measure, ordered that the CEC shall be appointed by a Committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India.

stories.headline: RBI MPC Meeting October 2026: Repo rate hike will be decided by these 5 factors | Explained
stories.title: RBI MPC Meeting October 2026: Repo rate hike will be decided by these 5 factors | Explained
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% for the last four consecutive policy meetings, after cutting it by a cumulative 125 basis points in 2025.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence

event term: 'repo rate' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: RBI MPC Meeting October 2026: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will meet from October 5 to 7 to review economic conditions and determine the next course of monetary policy.
The MPC’s decision is scheduled to be announced on October 7, with investors closely tracking the possibility of a repo rate hike—the first such increase since February 2023.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% for the last four consecutive policy meetings, after cutting it by a cumulative 125 basis points in 2025.

However, rising inflation, higher energy prices and rate hikes by several major global central banks have strengthened expectations that the RBI may shift towards a tighter monetary policy stance in October.
Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could consider a 25 basis point increase in the repo rate, taking it to 5.50%.

If the hike materialises, it would be the central bank’s first rate increase since February 2023 and could signal a shift towards a tighter monetary policy stance amid changing inflation and economic conditions.
Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research at Brickwork Ratings, said the RBI, after maintaining rates through 2026, is facing increasing pressure to raise the repo rate at its October policy review.
He said a 25 basis point hike to 5.50% has become a realistic possibility, marking the first increase since early 2023.
“The arguments for a rate hike have gained strength, with retail inflation rising to 4.82% and expected to peak during the festive quarter.
Crude oil prices remain above $100 a barrel, the rupee has weakened beyond 96, and the Fed’s recent rate hike has narrowed the interest-rate differential, adding to pressure on the currency.

However, inflation remains within the RBI’s target range and price pressures have yet to become broad-based, which could prompt the MPC to hold rates once again while adopting a firmly hawkish stance.
In either scenario, a rate cut appears unlikely for now, with the next policy move more likely to be a hike than a reduction,” Sharan said.
